hook_text: A crane that winds beautifully and then folds in half scores the same as one that never winds at all. You need both halves of the year.
clip_script: Two sheets, one crane. Sheet one: mechanical advantage, load over effort. Crank: handle over drum, about six. Pulley at the tip: one. Total six, and your finger moves six times as far as the magnet. Sheet two: frames. They fail three ways. Bend: so roll the card into a tube. Fold: so put a diagonal across every rectangle. Tip: so widen the base and put the cells at the back. Now take your sketch and walk it. From the magnet backwards: string, pulley, arm, joint, mast, base, asking will it hold. From the hand forwards: handle, drum, string, pulley, magnet, asking what is the advantage. Write the numbers on one side and the stiffeners on the other. That is one page that proves you understood two terms.
visual_style: Whiteboard split in two; numbers chaining to a total on the left; a rectangle gaining a diagonal and a strip rolling into a tube on the right; a crane sketch with arrows walking both ways.
mood: Steady and summarising, pulling threads together.
pacing: Sheet one, sheet two, walk back, walk forward, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and walk both paths on your own crane sketch.
